calc.482: Do foreign workers cost more than Turkish workers?
calc.483: On payroll, no. The gross salary and the SGK payments are the same, because Turkish labour law treats both workers the same way. The extra cost is paid only once: permit and card fees of about ₺16,000 per worker for each permit period, plus travel if you pay for it. Over a contract of several years, the difference per month is small.
calc.484: Is there a legal minimum salary for foreign workers?
calc.485: Yes. Every job has a minimum gross salary, set as a multiple of the minimum wage: 1× for unskilled jobs, 1.5× for skilled and specialist jobs, and more for engineers and managers. If you offer less, the permit is refused, so this calculator does not let you go below the minimum for the job you choose.
calc.486: Who pays the flight and the accommodation?
calc.487: You decide this together and write it in the contract. Most of our employers pay the one-way flight and give shared accommodation, especially in construction, farming and hotels, because workers stay longer that way. For most jobs the law does not require either.
calc.488: Do government SGK incentives apply to foreign workers too?
calc.489: The ones given to the workplace do. The 5510 premium discount and the minimum wage support are given to your workplace and depend on your own SGK record, not on the worker's nationality, so they work the same way for a foreign worker. Incentives that need the person to be registered as unemployed at İŞKUR, such as 7103 / geçici 19, cannot be used, because a foreign worker cannot have that registration. Since everything depends on your own SGK record, we always quote the full price without discounts and let your accountant confirm the saving.
calc.490: Is there a limit on how many foreign workers we can employ?
calc.491: Yes. As a rule the Ministry wants five Turkish employees registered with SGK at that workplace for every foreign worker. Some cases are exempt: certified tourism and hotel businesses with at least ten Turkish employees, workplaces with net sales of ₺50 million or more (up to five foreign workers), household services, and people who have lived legally in Turkey for three of the last five years. Use the quota check above for your own numbers. We confirm any exemption in writing before we file an application.
calc.492: Is there government funding for hiring foreign workers, in agriculture or any other sector?
calc.493: No. Turkey gives no grant, refund or wage support for employing a foreign worker, in farming or in any other sector. Farming supports (tarımsal destekler) are paid to the producer for production itself: land, diesel, seed and animals. They do not increase if you hire workers from abroad. The only state help here is the SGK premium discount and the minimum wage support, and you would get both for a Turkish employee too.
calc.494: Does our company itself have to meet any conditions?
calc.495: Yes, and this is separate from the 5:1 rule. Your company must meet at least one of these: ₺100,000 paid-in capital, ₺800,000 gross sales last year, or $250,000 of exports. One of them is enough. Household employers and a few exempt groups do not have to meet this. Many companies fail here without expecting it, so check it before you open a file. The pass check on this page takes you through it.
calc.496: What happens if we employ someone without a permit?
calc.497: Under Law No. 6735 the employer pays a fine of ₺102,504 for each foreign worker found without a permit in 2026, and double that if it happens again. You must also pay the worker's accommodation, return travel and health costs, including for the spouse and children. The worker gets a separate fine and is reported for deportation. On top of this, your workplace loses all SGK incentives for one month, or for one year if it happens again within three years. One fine costs more than doing everything legally.
calc.498: Can we employ a foreign student who is already studying here?
calc.499: Yes, with a work permit that you apply for. The student cannot apply alone. Associate and bachelor students can work only after their first year, and only part-time, up to 24 hours a week. Some students on state scholarships cannot work at all while studying. Master's and doctorate students have no such limits: they can work from any point in their studies, with no hour limit. Their student residence permit must stay valid all the time, because the work permit does not replace it. One thing employers often get wrong: student years do not count for the three-of-five-years exemption, so a new graduate's first normal work permit follows the standard rules.
calc.500: Can we claim KOSGEB or similar support for a foreign employee's wages?
calc.501: No. KOSGEB's qualified-personnel salary support is only for Turkish citizens with a university degree, and foreign workers are named in the list of people who cannot be employed under it, together with retirees and the owner's own family. KOSGEB's other programmes support the business itself (investment, machinery, digital work, training) and none of them pay part of a worker's wage. If your accountant already has a KOSGEB employment commitment, foreign workers still count in your total SGK staff number, but not in the personnel support payment.
calc.502: We only need workers for the 6-month season — does that change the cost?
calc.503: The monthly cost is the same, but the one-time costs are shared over fewer months. Permit fees and flights are paid once, whether the contract is six months or three years, so the cost per month is higher for a season. Set the contract length to 6 months in the calculator and you see that figure. For very short work there is also the work permit exemption route, which avoids the full permit process. calc.504: Are the permit fees per year or one-off?
calc.505: Per permit period. The first permit is usually one year, the first extension two years and the next three years. You pay the fee again at each renewal, not every year.
